title: Baseline — plain Cothas in milk. The cup that disappeared.
body: First structured baseline session. 2g Cothas Royal Blend in 125g milk, just off boiling. Stirred 20 seconds. Smelled it before drinking — mostly milk. Nothing assertive. Drank two sips before food, a few more with poha, finished the rest 15 minutes later. Throughout: smooth, flat, not unpleasant. The chicory softened everything but also erased everything. Towards the end I could faintly detect the chicory itself — slightly bitter, slightly woody. That was the only distinctive moment in the entire cup. Compared to Mocha Farms, which gives me a physical jolt within minutes, this gave nothing I could name. Functionally: slight wakefulness, marginally better focus, but I had already been thinking about the experiment before drinking, so psychological contamination likely. This cup did not fail. It showed me what Cothas needs around it to become alive.
observations: 2g Cothas Royal Blend, 125ml milk just off boiling
Aroma: almost entirely milk — no coffee presence
Taste: smooth, flat, chicory detectable only at the end
Body: 5/10 — medium-light, not uncomfortable
Aftertaste: 5–10 seconds, then gone
No acidity, no bitterness, no distinctive character
Better than Nescafe instant — but not by much on its own
note: The cup disappeared into the milk. Cothas alone cannot carry a ritual.

title: RUKH v2 — the cup stopped feeling flat.
body: Changed three variables from yesterday: increased coffee to 2.5g, reduced milk to 80ml, dissolved coffee in 38ml hot water first before adding milk. Added 0.2g pre-ground cardamom — full pod including green shell. As I brought the cup to my mouth, the aroma felt like cardamom tea. But when I drank it, it resolved into coffee. That contrast was confusing at first, then interesting. The cup had shape now. Texture was noticeably thicker despite adding water — better extraction architecture explains this. Bitterness softened. Chicory integrated rather than sitting separately. Cardamom overpowered the coffee aromatically and partially in taste. But instead of making the drink worse, it created a stronger sensory identity. The drink felt warmer, fuller, more alive. Functionally cleaner than yesterday — alertness increased within minutes, sleepiness reduced, mood lifted slightly. Alert window extended to approximately 90 minutes before any decline. Most important shift: this no longer felt like instant coffee with milk. It felt like an intentional beverage.
observations: Cothas 2.5g, water 38ml first, then 80ml milk at warm-hot
Cardamom 0.2g full pod powder — green shell included
Aroma: cardamom tea on nose, coffee on palate — memorable contrast
Texture: noticeably thicker than yesterday despite more liquid
Body: 7/10 — significant improvement
Cardamom currently overpowering — seeds-only tomorrow
Alert window: ~90 min vs earlier decline yesterday
Woke 5AM, 6hrs sleep, 1.5hrs deep work before cup — context was better
note: It smelled like cardamom chai, but drank like coffee. That contrast is not a flaw — it is identity.

title: RUKH v3 — cinnamon took the steering wheel.
body: Broke my own rule today. Introduced cinnamon 0.25g the same day I was supposed to only refine the cardamom. Also used freshly powdered cardamom seeds only at 0.2g — which was an improvement in form, though the quantity was still high. Cinnamon completely dominated the aroma. Coffee was barely detectable before milk. After milk, aroma went flat again with cinnamon still present. The drink felt relaxing rather than activating — a warm, grounded quality that was pleasant but wrong for a midday focus cup. Functional scores improved minimally: 0.5 points across most metrics. Yesterday's 2-point alertness uplift did not happen today. Unclear whether this is the cinnamon's calming properties or 4 hours of sleep from a difficult night with my daughter — most likely the sleep. One important discovery: cardamom powder left sediment at the bottom that concentrated into a strong cardamom finish at the end. The last two sips were almost entirely cardamom. This is a preparation problem — coarser crush needed. Or water infusion method. Lesson relearned: one variable per day. I already knew this. Now I have felt the cost of ignoring it.
observations: Cothas 2.5g, cardamom seeds only 0.2g, cinnamon 0.25g — two variables changed
Woke 3:30AM after 4hrs sleep — high confounder day
Cinnamon dominated aroma completely before and after milk
Emotional direction: warm, grounded, slower — opposite of activation
Cardamom sediment accumulated at bottom — final sips were only cardamom
Functional uplift minimal: 0.5 pts across metrics
Cinnamon appears to create relaxing rather than activating direction
note: Cinnamon took the steering wheel. One variable per day. I knew this. Now I have felt the cost.

title: KISSE v1 — too many things shouting at once.
body: First attempt at the evening ritual cup. Prepared for my brother-in-law arriving post-swim on a rainy evening. Cothas Royal Blend 2.6g, cardamom 0.15g full pod powder, cinnamon 0.5g, cacao 3g, coconut jaggery 1g, black pepper pinch. 100ml hot water, stirred 30 seconds, 20ml warm milk. He found it immediately bitter. Cardamom and cinnamon overpowering. He was having it with an avocado sandwich which amplified the bitterness further. Did not finish the cup. The problem was clear in hindsight: five competing flavour systems at full intensity simultaneously. Cacao, coffee, cardamom, cinnamon, pepper — all asserting themselves, none yielding. Nothing had hierarchy. Made a second cup immediately — Levista 80/20 instead of Cothas, cardamom reduced to 0.1g, cinnamon to 0.3g, cacao increased to 3.5g. He and I shared it. This version was different. Cacao took control. Coffee became structural rather than dominant. I found it close to the hot cacao drink I had in Mexico. He found it significantly more drinkable. I would have this as a conversational drink.
observations: Version 1 — Cothas 2.6g: bitter, spices competing, abandoned with food
Version 2 — Levista 80/20 2.5g: cacao-led, coffee structural, drinkable
Levista integrates better than Cothas — chicory softens bitterness
Avocado sandwich amplified bitterness significantly — KISSE needs standalone moment
Cacao at 3–3.5g restructures the drink entirely — coffee becomes background
Mexico hot cacao comparison emerged naturally
Brother-in-law trajectory: difficult → improved across the session
note: KISSE is not a coffee-first drink. It is a cacao ritual that uses coffee structurally.

title: KISSE v2 — warmer, slower, closer.
body: Revised recipe based on yesterday's learning. Levista 80/20 confirmed as the base. Reduced all spices dramatically. Cacao held at 3g. Added coconut sugar as bitterness buffer. Preparation sequence refined: warm cup first, dry ingredients in order starting with cacao, hot water at 85°C, 35-second stir, 25-second rest, 20ml warm milk with one gentle stir only. Served to brother-in-law again — same tester, which means I now have a progression across three sessions with the same palate as reference. His feedback: cinnamon and cardamom impact noticeably less than yesterday. Not bitter. Can slightly sense the jaggery. Yesterday was difficult to drink, today significantly easier. Thickness appropriate for a conversational cup. His friend tasted it for the first time — guessed hazelnut initially, then said it felt like kadha. The hazelnut association comes from Maillard compounds in dark coffee combining with cacao. Sophisticated palate. The kadha association is interesting — both a risk and a signal. Functionally: no adaptogen in this SKU, so I was not measuring state change. Felt relaxed, conversational, unhurried. The cup encouraged slower pace.
observations: Levista 80/20 2.2g confirmed as correct base
Cacao 3g — cacao-led character confirmed
Spices dramatically reduced from v1
Coconut sugar 1.2g — essential bitterness buffer
Brother-in-law progression: difficult → improved → significantly better
Friend: hazelnut first guess (sophisticated), kadha second (ritual association)
Post-swim, rainy evening — context perfect for this SKU
Drink slows the pace naturally — satiety effect from cacao noted
note: It could keep me in that mood. That is not a flavour note. That is positioning.

title: KISSE v3 — the preparation ritual matters as much as the drink.
body: Third iteration. Same Levista base, same cacao quantity, refined preparation sequence. Two testers this time — brother-in-law and his friend, same friend who mentioned kadha yesterday. They were in a hurry — 10 minutes before leaving for somewhere. This matters because KISSE is explicitly a slow drink and rushed testers produce unreliable data. Still, the feedback trajectory continued upward. Compared to yesterday: cardamom and cinnamon impact even more controlled, no bitterness, jaggery detectable, thickness described as appropriate for conversation purpose. The same friend who said kadha yesterday did not say it again today — which suggests the spice reduction moved it out of medicinal territory. Still not fully where it needs to be, but the direction is right.
observations: Testers in a hurry — 10-minute feedback window, data quality lower than ideal
Cinnamon and cardamom noticeably less dominant than v2
No bitterness reported
Jaggery now detectable — sweetness integrated
Thickness confirmed as appropriate for conversational format
Kadha association not repeated by friend — moved out of medicinal territory
Preparation ritual: warming cup first, layered dry ingredients, 35s stir, rest, milk
note: Three sessions, same tester. The trajectory from difficult to drinkable to appropriate is real data.

title: KISSE v4 — removed cardamom, found the cafe mocha.
body: Personal iteration after the guest session. Wanted to understand what KISSE becomes without cardamom and pepper. Levista 80/20 2.6g, cacao 2.25g (reduced), cinnamon 0.25g, coconut jaggery 1.25g. No cardamom. No black pepper. 100ml hot water, 30 second stir, 20 second rest, 20ml milk. Result: aroma shifted entirely to hot chocolate. Lost the Indian identity immediately. Taste was surprisingly more bitter than v3 despite reduced cacao — possibly because cardamom was providing a bitterness-buffering function I had not accounted for. Cacao did not dissolve fully — powdery texture in the mouth. Feels like cafe mocha. More internationally familiar, less distinctly Indian. Good drink. Not KISSE. The lesson: cardamom is not optional. It is not just a flavour — it is the ingredient that marks this as Indian rather than generically cacao. Remove it and the drink loses its cultural coordinates. The dissolution problem needs solving with Dutch-processed cacao for this SKU.
observations: No cardamom, no black pepper — lost Indian identity immediately
Aroma: hot chocolate — internationally familiar, not distinctive
Taste: surprisingly more bitter than v3 despite less cacao
Cacao undissolved — powdery texture in mouth throughout
Cafe mocha comparison accurate — not what KISSE should be
Cardamom appears to buffer bitterness as well as provide aroma
Dutch-processed cacao needed for dissolution — order separately
Ate dry fruits and fox nuts before — felt full halfway through cup
note: Removed cardamom and found a cafe mocha. Cardamom is what makes this Indian. It is not optional.
